images.title: Cutting the unit again
images.purpose: Show that the same unit from 0 to 1 can be cut into more and more equal parts, and each new cut brings new fractions between 0 and 1.
images.composition: Three number lines of exactly the same length stacked one under another with wide gaps between them, sharing one 0 and one 1, and one question below.
images.exact_structure: Three grey #6B7280 number lines, each from 0 to 1 and exactly the same length, left ends and right ends aligned. Two thin dashed grey vertical guides pass through all left ends and all right ends; 0 sits once at the top of the left guide, 1 once at the top of the right guide. Top line: 3 evenly spaced ticks, 2 equal parts, teal #0072B2. Middle: 5 ticks, 4 equal parts, amber #E69F00. Bottom: 9 ticks, 8 equal parts, reddish purple #CC79A7. Exactly 3 lines.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
number lines of different lengths, or any count or word giving how many fractions there are
images.takeaway: Cutting the unit into more equal parts gives new fractions between 0 and 1.
images.description: Three same-length number lines from 0 to 1, cut into 2, 4 and 8 equal parts, with the question how many fractions fit between 0 and 1.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say what the next line would be cut into, and whether the cutting ever has to stop.

image_decisions.why: Stacked lines cut finer and finer pose the question visually without stating the answer.
